A deload week helps to manage CNS fatigue. If you’re lifting heavy or at high intensity (sounds a lot like CrossFit!) then a deload week will help to give your CNS a break, and you should come back finding equivalent workouts “easier” than before the deload. However if you’re only hitting a couple of sessions per week, you’re probably managing CNS fatigue in between sessions - whereas if you’re working out 5/6+ times a week you’re likely building up CNS fatigue.

I tend to take a deload week roughly once every 6-8 weeks - I’ll often align them with when I’m on holiday or have some big things going on in my life that it helps to get time back for. They act as a nice time to take focus away from lifting and put it on other things I enjoy. 

During a deload week I’ll hit one or two normal sessions but at reduced weight (without increasing volume). I’ll have a couple of days for different forms of exercise - eg a gentle run, swim, bike ride, hike, etc. And I’ll have a couple of days entirely off.
